## So what is the composable unit?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
- A `Distributions.jl` distribution is already an interface the whole
  of Julia understands, so write the epidemiology as distributions and
  the probabilistic programming language becomes optional
- `CensoredDistributions.jl` does not depend on Turing. Nothing in
  `src/` mentions it
- A composed delay comes back as a plain distribution type, and the
  generic functions still work on it

```julia
# a serial interval, censored and truncated
si = double_interval_censored(
  convolve_distributions(generation_time, incubation);
  upper = 15, interval = 1)
```

::: {.attribution}
`CensoredDistributions.jl` v0.2.22, run for this talk,
`scripts/composable-composed-type.jl`. `cdf(si, 5.0)` returns `0.094`
on that type, so the generic functions did not need telling about it
:::
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**And what comes back**

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {'flowchart': {'rankSpacing': 32}}}%%
flowchart TB
  ic["IntervalCensored"] --> tr["Truncated"]
  tr --> pc["PrimaryCensored"]
  pc --> cv["Convolved"]
  cv --> gt["Gamma"]
  cv --> inc["LogNormal"]
```

::: {.attribution}
The nesting is the type printed by that script, with the parameter
types dropped. Reading down, daily reporting wraps the cutoff at 15,
which wraps the primary window, which wraps the two delays
:::
:::
::::

## How far does that go?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
| Piece of a model | Is it a distribution? |
|---|---|
| Delay, censored and truncated | Yes, today |
| Renewal process | No |
| ARIMA latent process | No |
| ODE | No |
| The fitting layer | No |

: {tbl-colwidths="[55,45]"}
:::
::: {.column width="4%"}
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
::: {.callout-important}
The delay half of this deck has a story. The time series half does not,
and neither does the fitting layer, which is what the probabilistic
programming language was doing.
:::

- So this is a direction, not a plan. It would need a way to write a
  time series as a distribution, and a way to fit one without a model
  macro

::: {.attribution}
`CensoredDistributions.jl` v0.2.22, `main` checked 2026-08-10. A
`DynamicPPL` package extension exists on an unmerged branch, not on
`main`. Open issue `CensoredDistributions.jl#749` says the joint fit is
too slow, because reverse mode autodiff through `cdf(Convolved(...))`
costs too much per step. The delay side of this is written up in full at
[samabbott.co.uk/JuliaCon2026/delays][delays-talk]
:::
:::
::::

## Other ways to compose models

+------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
| Approach                     | How it composes                     |
+==============================+=====================================+
| AlgebraicJulia               | Formal compositional guarantees,    |
|                              | and little support for              |
|                              | probabilistic models                |
+------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
| `JuliaBUGS.jl`, `RxInfer.jl` | Models specified as graphs          |
+------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
| `ModelingToolkit.jl`         | Acausal components, symbolically    |
+------------------------------+-------------------------------------+
| `Gen.jl`                     | Nested generative functions, at a   |
|                              | lower level than Turing.jl          |
+------------------------------+-------------------------------------+

::: {.attribution}
The paper's discussion of alternative designs,
[doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17884675](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17884675)
:::
